title: Scale-Shift and Fractional Fourier Transform as Rotations over Finite Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The framed substrate: the Subject $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$ with $\p=4\kap+1$, its register $\pi=2\kap$, $\im=-\gen^{\kap}=\gen^{-\kap}$, $e=\gen^{\im}$; the frame-relative labels and the atlas of presentations $\gen\mapsto\gen^{u}$; time as scale-dilation, the generator as the observer's own advance.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The Weil representation $\omega_\p$ of $\SL(2,\Fp)$ and its Schr\"odinger model, the finite Fourier transform representing the rotation $w$, the finite harmonic oscillator; the scalar convention $\omega_\p(w)^{2}=\omega_\p(-I)$, $\omega_\p(w)^{4}=I$.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The classical evaluation of the twisted quadratic Gauss sum for $4\mid n$, $\sum_k\zeta_n^{uk^{2}}=\bigl(\tfrac{\kap}{u}\bigr)(1\pm i)\sqrt n$; the eigenvalue quartet of prime-modulus number-theoretic transforms; the multiplicity counts of the discrete Fourier eigenvalues.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The entropic uncertainty relation for a pair of bases, $H_{B}+H_{B'}\ge-2\log c$, $c$ the maximal overlap, $c=n^{-1/2}$ for mutually unbiased bases, saturated by basis-localized states.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The framed-rational zoom: the grids $G_n$ and their $(\p-1)$-periodicity $G_{n+(\p-1)}=G_n$, the meridian shift $m\mapsto m-1$ as the refinement step.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: The measurement layer: probabilities are structural weights of the cyclotomic stratum, the finite-field module carries no Born magnitude, and the readout is an observer-side declaration; the shell dynamics a bijection, entropy attaching to the readout.

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: The continuum fractional Fourier transform and the finite constructions the family is separated from: the eigenbasis and matrix-function transforms, the harmonic-oscillator propagator reading.

blocks.title: The shell: the frame datum and the Fourier operator

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: Shell data, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$, the meridian cycle $\Phit=\Z_{4\kap}$, the oriented quarter-turn $\im=-\gen^{\kap}$ (clockwise phase convention), $\pi=2\kap$, $e=\gen^{\im}$; the meridians $M_s=\{a\gen^{s}:a\in I_\p\}$; the six shells of Table~\ref{tab:checks} with their generators and quarter-turns.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: The Euler identity is a property of the chart class: $e^{\im\pi}=\gen^{2\kap(\im\bmod2)}\equiv-1$ exactly when the quarter-turn residue is odd; the conjugate reframing $(\gen,\im)\mapsto(\gen^{-1},-\im)$ toggles the parity, so one member of each conjugate pair carries it; on $\F_{13}(\chron;0,1,2)$, $\im=5$ and $6^{6}=-1$. Every primitive frame of the six shells.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: Chart covariance: under $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $u\in\Zp^{\times}$, the quarter-turn name flips exactly on $u\equiv3\pmod4$ and the exponential-unit name moves already at $u\equiv1\pmod4$ whenever $\im(u-1)\not\equiv0\pmod{4\kap}$ ($\p=13$, $u=5$: $e'=2\neq6$); the registered objects (C3, C4, C9, F3) are invariant.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The shell Fourier matrix $\Wt_{kj}=\gen^{jk}$ on $\Vt=\Fp^{\Phit}$, the reversal $J$, the normalized shell Fourier operator $\Ft=\im\Wt$.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: $\Wt^{2}=-J$, $\Ft^{2}=J$, $\Ft^{4}=I$: the normalized operator generates the four-cycle, on the six shells of Table~\ref{tab:checks}.

rows.label: B6
rows.predicate: The normalization is the unitary constant read in the field: $1/n\equiv-1$, its square roots in $\Fp$ are exactly $\pm\im$, and $(c\Wt)^{2}=J$ if and only if $c=\pm\im$.

rows.label: B7
rows.predicate: $\Wt J=J\Wt$, hence $\Ft J=J\Ft$; $\Vt=V^{+}\oplus V^{-}$ with $\dim V^{+}=2\kap+1$, $\dim V^{-}=2\kap-1$.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The projectors $\Pi_\ell=\tfrac14\sum_{r=0}^{3}\im^{-\ell r}\Ft^{r}$ and the principal framed character lift $\Ft^{[s]}=\sum_\ell\gen^{-\ell s}\Pi_\ell$, $s\in\Phit$: the refinement base is the inverse generator, $(\gen^{-1})^{\kap}=\im$, each projector's character the $\ell$-th power of the meridian phase $z_s=\gen^{-s}$.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: $\Pi_\ell^{2}=\Pi_\ell$, $\Pi_\ell\Pi_m=0$ for $\ell\neq m$, $\sum_\ell\Pi_\ell=I$, $\Ft\Pi_\ell=\im^{\ell}\Pi_\ell$.

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The exact finite-field FrFT: $s\mapsto\Ft^{[s]}$ is a representation of $\Phit$, $\Ft^{[s+r]}=\Ft^{[s]}\Ft^{[r]}$ on every pair of the six shells, with the cardinal values $\Ft^{[0]}=I$, $\Ft^{[\kap]}=\Ft$, $\Ft^{[2\kap]}=J$, $\Ft^{[3\kap]}=\Ft^{-1}$, and $(\Ft^{[1]})^{\kap}=\Ft$.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Faithfulness: $s\mapsto\Ft^{[s]}$ is injective on $\Z_{4\kap}$ for every $\kap\ge1$; at $\p=5$ the surviving odd projector carries the faithful character.

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: The multiplicities $m_\ell=\operatorname{rank}\Pi_\ell=\dim\ker(\Ft-\im^{\ell}I)$: $m_0+m_2=2\kap+1$, $m_1+m_3=2\kap-1$; $m_0,m_2\ge1$; $m_1,m_3\ge1$ for $\kap\ge2$; at $\p=5$ exactly one of $\Pi_1,\Pi_3$ vanishes.

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: Multiplicities are chart data: the vertex relabelling $m\mapsto um$ carries $\Ft(\gen)$ to $\Ft(\gen^{u^{2}})$ by a coordinate permutation; at $\p=13$ the frames $\gen=2$ and $\gen=6$ give $(3,3,4,2)$ and $(4,2,3,3)$, traces $4$ and $9$.

rows.label: C7
rows.predicate: The multiplicity dichotomy: $G=\sum_{k}\gen^{k^{2}}=\varepsilon(1+\im)$; the tuple is $(\kap,\kap,\kap+1,\kap-1)$ for $\varepsilon=+1$ and $(\kap+1,\kap-1,\kap,\kap)$ for $\varepsilon=-1$; $\varepsilon(\gen^{-1})=-\varepsilon(\gen)$, $\varepsilon(\gen^{u})=\bigl(\tfrac{\kap}{u}\bigr)\varepsilon(\gen)$ for $u\equiv1\pmod4$, the two classes equally populated; the proof's identities $GG^{*}=-2$, $G^{2}=2\im$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Ft=\im G$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Ft^{2}=2$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Ft^{3}=\im G^{*}$. Exact on the $38$ primitive frames of $\p\in\{5,13,17,29,37\}$ and the $16$ of $\p=41$.

rows.label: C8
rows.predicate: Classification: every exponent lift $a_\ell\equiv\ell\pmod4$ is additive with the same cardinal skeleton; a family canonical in the chart $\gen^{u}$ with $u^{2}\not\equiv1\pmod{4\kap}$ does not commute with $\Ft$ ($\p=29$, $u=5$, and every such chart of the six shells); the principal lift is the unique power-tower member.

rows.label: C9
rows.predicate: The conjugate reframing $(\gen,\im)\mapsto(\gen^{-1},-\im)$: exactly $\Ft'=-\Ft^{-1}$ and $\Pi'_\ell=\Pi_{\ell+2}$; the operator relations, cardinal values, additivity and faithfulness hold on the conjugate frame, and its multiplicity tuple is the other pattern of C7.

blocks.title: Representation domains and the coordinate-side zoom

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The meridional representation domain $D_s=(\Vt,\mathcal B_s)$, $\mathcal B_s=\Ft^{[s]}\mathcal B_0$, every $\Ft^{[s]}$ invertible; the cardinal domains spatial, spectral, parity, inverse-spectral.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: The $4\kap$ framed domains are pairwise distinct; read as unordered measurement bases $B_{s+2\kap}=B_s$, since $\Ft^{[s+2\kap]}=\Ft^{[s]}J$ and $J$ permutes the standard basis, and the cycle carries exactly $2\kap$ of them.

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: The meridian-step interval $I_\p=\{0,1,\dots,\pi\}$, the meridian-scale map $S_r(x)=\gen^{r}x$, and the local scale chart $\gen\mapsto\lambda>1$ reading the effective step $\gen^{m}$ as $\lambda^{m}$ [chart].

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: Meridian-scale covariance: $S_r(M_m)=M_{m+r}$ for every $(m,r)$, as ordered lists; consecutive entries of $M_m$ differ by the effective step $\gen^{m}$; $S_{r+(\p-1)}=S_r$, the periodicity of A5 in meridian form.

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: Meridian zoom [chart]: $M_m$ reads the meridian-coordinate vector at step $\lambda^{\tilde m}$, the forward shift zoom-out and the inverse shift zoom-in, the seam an aliasing return; at $\p=13$, $\gen=2$ the ladder $M_0,\dots,M_3$ at steps $1,2,4,8$, unwrapped within $w\gen^{r}<\p$ ($w=\pi=6$: $r\le1$) and wrapping from $M_2$.

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: Scope of the unification: the representation-side rotation and the coordinate-side scale shift act on carriers of different dimension and are not equal as operators; they share the index group $\Phit$ and the cardinal labels, and the operator-level relation is E5--E7.

blocks.title: The Weil dictionary and the operator-level comparison

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The Weil-side data: $z_s=\gen^{-s}$, $c_s=(z_s+z_s^{-1})/2$, $d_s=(z_s-z_s^{-1})/(2\im)$, the rotation $R_s$; the pulled-back family $\operatorname{FrFT}^{\rm Weil}_\kap(s)=\omega_\p(R_s)$; cardinal Weil correspondence of two families.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: $R_s\in SO(2,\Fp)$, and $s\mapsto R_s$ is an isomorphism $\Phit\simeq SO(2,\Fp)$ with $|SO(2,\Fp)|=\p-1=4\kap$: the full rotation group of the $\p^{2}$-point plane is the meridian cycle.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: The cardinal-skeleton dictionary $M_s\leftrightarrow s\leftrightarrow z_s\leftrightarrow R_s$ with $R_0=I$, $R_\kap=w$, $R_{2\kap}=-I$, $R_{3\kap}=w^{-1}$ (the $R_\kap$ column of Table~\ref{tab:checks}), $z_\kap=\im$; the FRC-native and Weil families stand in cardinal Weil correspondence, the Weil side by the normalization of A2.

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: Scope and reading of the dictionary: agreement on the four cardinal indices only, the two families acting on spaces of different dimension over different coefficient rings; the holographic reading, the rotation symmetry of the $\p^{2}$-point plane carried by a cycle of the size of its square root, the state side of dimension $\p$.

rows.label: E5
rows.predicate: Spectral obstruction: the exponent shift $\sigma$ has the $4\kap$ simple eigenvalues $\Fpx$, every $\Ft^{[s]}$ at most four; for $\kap\ge2$ the cyclic groups $\langle\sigma\rangle$ and $\langle\Ft^{[1]}\rangle$ are not conjugate.

rows.label: E6
rows.predicate: Common character sector: on $E_1=\operatorname{im}\Pi_1\neq0$ ($\kap\ge2$) $\Ft^{[s]}=\gen^{-s}I$, the intertwiner $\Ft^{[s]}T_v=T_vS_{-s}$ on every $x\in\Fp$ and $s$, and $R_s(1,-\im)^{\mathsf T}=\gen^{-s}(1,-\im)^{\mathsf T}$.

rows.label: E7
rows.predicate: Cardinal Heisenberg covariance: $\Ft\sigma\Ft^{-1}=D_1$, $\Ft D_1\Ft^{-1}=\sigma^{-1}$; $\Ft^{r}\sigma=\sigma_r\Ft^{r}$ with $(\sigma,D_1,\sigma^{-1},D_1^{-1})$; the expansion \eqref{eq:conj-expansion}; $\Ft^{[s]}\sigma\Ft^{[s]-1}$ monomial exactly at the four cardinal indices and non-monomial at every one of the $112$ intermediate indices of $\p\in\{13,17,29,37,41\}$.

rows.label: E8
rows.predicate: Cardinal exclusivity: for every $s\notin\{0,\kap,2\kap,3\kap\}$ the operator \eqref{eq:conj-expansion} is not monomial --- off $j\in\{-1,0,1\}$ its row $0$ is $x^{-1}$ times a quadratic in $x=\gen^{j}$ with leading coefficient $\im\,[c_0(s)+c_2(s)]\,c_3(-s)\neq0$, $c_0(s)+c_2(s)=\tfrac12(1+\gen^{-2s})$, so the row has at least $4\kap-5$ nonzero entries; the count checked on every shell below $200$.

blocks.title: The cyclotomic observer readout and the entropy cycle

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: The readout algebra $A=\Z[\tfrac{1}{4n},X,Y,Y^{-1}]/(\Phi_n(X),Y^{2}-n)$ with the continuum chart $\sigma_\C$ ($X\mapsto\zeta_n$, $Y\mapsto+\sqrt n$) and the framed reduction $\rho$ ($X\mapsto\gen$, $Y\mapsto-\im$); the readout of a shell state as the Born vector of a selected lift, its Shannon entropy in nats, not thermodynamic.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: $\widehat G^{2}=2n\,X^{\kap}$ in $A$, exact modulo $\Phi_n(X)$; under $\sigma_\C$, $(\sum_k\zeta_n^{k^{2}})^{2}=2n\,i$; under $\rho$, $G^{2}=2\im$, the reduction the proof of C7 uses.

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: Entropic cardinal values $H(0)=H(2\kap)=0$, $H(\kap)=H(3\kap)=\log n$ for every site-localized input; $B_0$ and $B_\kap$ mutually unbiased, $H_{B_0}+H_{B_\kap}\ge\log n$ saturated by the localized states and by the comb $(\delta_0+\delta_6)/\sqrt2$ at $n=12$, $\log2+\log6=\log12$ [approx].

rows.label: F4
rows.predicate: The closed form for $\delta_0$: $p_0=1-\tfrac{n-1}{n}t_s$, $p_{j\neq0}=t_s/n$, $t_s=(2-\zeta_n^{2s}-\zeta_n^{-2s})/4$, read as $\sin^{2}(\pi s/2\kap)$; $H(s)$ strictly increasing on $[0,\kap]$, two oscillations per cycle, strictly intermediate off the cardinal indices [approx].

rows.label: F5
rows.predicate: $\p=13$: $H(s)/\log n=0,\,.44,\,.91,\,1,\,.91,\,.44$ over each half-cycle; Figure~\ref{fig:entropy13} regenerated [approx].

rows.label: F6
rows.predicate: Input dependence: $\delta_1$ gives $H(1)/\log n=0.55$ against $0.44$ for $\delta_0$; $\delta_j$ meets the odd projectors exactly for $j\notin\{0,2\kap\}$, and $\delta_{2\kap}$ reproduces the $\delta_0$ curve [approx].

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: The Galois twist $X\mapsto\zeta_n^{u}$ relabels the $\delta_0$ curve by $s\mapsto us$ for every unit $u$ and leaves the cardinal values of every $\delta_j$ invariant; the conjugate twist $u=-1$ relabels the curve of every $\delta_j$, while for $j\notin\{0,2\kap\}$ a twist $u\not\equiv\pm1$ changes the intermediate curve ($n=12$, $\delta_1$, $u=5$: $0.55\mapsto0.44$ at $s=1$) [approx].

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.euler_identity
B2.doc: 2:D6, 6:B2, 00:C14 — the Euler identity on the shell: with `e = g^i` and `π = 2κ`, `(g^i)^{i·2κ} = (−1)^i` for every natural reading `i` of the quarter-turn — `−1` exactly when `i` is odd.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orientation_class
B3.doc: 2:D5, 6:B3, 13:B2 — the orientation classes: for `g' = g^u`, the quarter-turn `−g'^κ` is `−g^κ` when `u ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `−(−g^κ)` when `u ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

B5.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_relations
B5.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 — every shell: on a field with `p = 4κ + 1` elements, `n = p − 1`, `g` a primitive root and `F = i • W`: `W² = −J`, `F² = J`, `F⁴ = 1`, `W J = J W`.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.F_sq
B5.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 (`F² = J`, entrywise): the quarter-turn transform squares to the reversal.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.J_sq
B5.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 (`J² = 1`, entrywise): the reversal is an involution, so `F⁴ = J² = 1`.

B6.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.ofNat_n
B6.doc: 6:B6 — the normalization constant read in the field: `n = p − 1 ≡ −1`.

B7.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_relations
B7.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 — every shell: on a field with `p = 4κ + 1` elements, `n = p − 1`, `g` a primitive root and `F = i • W`: `W² = −J`, `F² = J`, `F⁴ = 1`, `W J = J W`.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.symm_antisymm_decomp
B7.doc: 6:B7 — the decomposition `V = V⁺ ⊕ V⁻`: with `h = 2⁻¹`, `v = v⁺ + v⁻` where `v⁺ k = h(v k + v (rev k))` is symmetric and `v⁻ k = h(v k − v (rev k))` antisymmetric; the decomposition is unique.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.symm_antisymm_unique
B7.doc: 6:B7 — the decomposition is unique: a vector that is both symmetric and antisymmetric is zero, so the symmetric and antisymmetric parts of `v` are determined.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.symm_determined
B7.doc: 6:B7 — a symmetric vector is determined by its `2κ + 1` coordinates `v 0, …, v (2κ)`.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.antisymm_determined
B7.doc: 6:B7 — an antisymmetric vector is determined by its `2κ − 1` coordinates `v 1, …, v (2κ − 1)`.

C2.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_proj
C2.doc: 6:C2 — on every shell: `F Π_ℓ = i^ℓ Π_ℓ`, `Π_ℓ Π_m = [ℓ = m] Π_ℓ`, `Σ_ℓ Π_ℓ = 1`.

C2.name: FRC.Fourier.proj_mul_proj
C2.doc: 6:C2 — the projectors are pairwise orthogonal idempotents: `Π_ℓ Π_m = [ℓ = m] Π_ℓ`.

C2.name: FRC.Fourier.sum_proj
C2.doc: 6:C2 — the projectors sum to the identity.

C3.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_frft_add
C3.doc: 6:C3 — additivity on every shell: `F^{[s+r]} = F^{[s]} F^{[r]}`, a representation of `ZMod (4κ)`.

C3.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_frft_cardinal
C3.doc: 6:C3 — the cardinal values on every shell: `F^{[mκ]} = F^m`, so `F^{[0]} = 1`, `F^{[κ]} = F`, `F^{[2κ]} = J`, `F^{[3κ]} = F³ = F⁻¹`, `F^{[4κ]} = 1`.

C3.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_frft_values
C3.doc: 6:C3 — `F^{[κ]} = F`, `F^{[2κ]} = J`, and the exact `κ`-th root `(F^{[1]})^κ = F`.

C4.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_frft_injective
C4.doc: 6:C4, 6:D2 — faithfulness on every shell: `s ↦ F^{[s]}` is injective on `ZMod (4κ)`, so the `4κ` fractional domains are distinct. For `κ ≥ 2` the odd projector `Π_1` is nonzero (C5); for `κ = 1` one of `Π_1`, `Π_3` is, and both indices are coprime to `4`.

C5.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_odd_proj_ne_zero
C5.doc: 6:C5 — `Π_1 ≠ 0` and `Π_3 ≠ 0` for `κ ≥ 2`: otherwise `e_1 − e_{−1}` would be an eigenvector of `F`.

C5.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_even_proj_ne_zero
C5.doc: 6:C5 — `Π_0 ≠ 0` and `Π_2 ≠ 0` for every `κ ≥ 1`: otherwise `e_0` would be an eigenvector of `F`.

C5.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_multiplicity_sums
C5.doc: 6:C5 — the multiplicity sums on the prime shell: `m_0 + m_2 = 2κ + 1` and `m_1 + m_3 = 2κ − 1`, with `m_ℓ = rank Π_ℓ`: the even and odd projector sums are the parity idempotents `(1 ± J)/2`, of traces `2κ + 1` and `2κ − 1`.

C7.name: FRC.Fourier.gauss_mul_gauss_inv
C7.doc: 6:C7 — `G G* = −2` in the field: `Σ_{k,l} g^{k²−l²} = Σ_d g^{d²} Σ_l g^{2ld}`, the inner geometric sum vanishing unless `2d = 0`, i.e. `d ∈ {0, 2κ}`, where it is `n ≡ −1`.

C7.name: FRC.Fourier.gauss_inv_of_sign
C7.doc: 6:C7 — the conjugate frame's sign: with `G = ε(1 + i)`, `ε = ±1`, the conjugate Gauss sum is `G* = G(g⁻¹) = −ε(1 + i')` for the conjugate quarter-turn `i' = −i`, so `ε(g⁻¹) = −ε(g)`.

C7.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_multiplicity_tuple
C7.doc: 6:C7 — the multiplicity tuple on the prime shell, as natural numbers: with `G = ε(1 + i)` (the classical evaluation, import A3), `(m_0, m_1, m_2, m_3) = (κ, κ, κ+1, κ−1)` for `ε = 1` and `(κ+1, κ−1, κ, κ)` for `ε = −1`.

C8.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_frftLift
C8.doc: 6:C8 — every exponent lift `a_ℓ ≡ ℓ (mod 4)` gives an additive family with the cardinal skeleton of the principal one, on every shell.

C9.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_conj
C9.doc: 6:C9 — the conjugate frame `(g⁻¹, −i)`: its transform is `F' = −F³ = −F⁻¹` (since `W(g⁻¹) = W J`), and its projectors are the shifted ones, `Π'_ℓ = Π_{ℓ+2}`.

D2.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_frft_injective
D2.doc: 6:C4, 6:D2 — faithfulness on every shell: `s ↦ F^{[s]}` is injective on `ZMod (4κ)`, so the `4κ` fractional domains are distinct. For `κ ≥ 2` the odd projector `Π_1` is nonzero (C5); for `κ = 1` one of `Π_1`, `Π_3` is, and both indices are coprime to `4`.

D2.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_frft_add_two_kappa
D2.doc: 6:D2 — `F^{[s+2κ]} = F^{[s]} J`: the framed domains `s` and `s + 2κ` differ by the parity involution, which permutes the standard basis (`mul_J_apply`), so they are one unordered measurement basis.

D2.name: FRC.Fourier.mul_J_apply
D2.doc: 6:D2 — `J` is a permutation matrix: `(M J) k j = M k (−j)`, so `M J` has the columns of `M`, reindexed by the parity involution `j ↦ −j`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.meridian_scale
D4.doc: 6:D4 — meridian-scale covariance: `S_r(M_m) = M_{m+r}` as ordered lists, for every `m, r`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.meridian_step
D4.doc: 6:D4 — the effective step: consecutive entries of `M_m` differ by `g^m`, `(a + 1) g^m = a g^m + g^m`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.scale_periodic
D4.doc: 6:D4 — `S_{r + (p−1)} = S_r`: the meridian-scale map is `(p − 1)`-periodic in `r` (the periodicity of the framed-rational zoom, A5).

D5.name: FRC.Shell.ladder13
D5.doc: 6:D5 — the `p = 13`, `g = 2`, `κ = 3` ladder: `M_0, M_1, M_2, M_3` at the effective steps `1, 2, 4, 8`; `M_0` and `M_1` are unwrapped (`π g^r = 6 g^r < 13` for `r ≤ 1`), `M_2` wraps (`6 · 4 = 24 ≥ 13`: its entries `0, 4, 8, 12, 3, 7, 11` return through the seam).

E2.name: FRC.Fourier.circle
E2.doc: 6:E2 — `R_s ∈ SO(2)`: `c² + d² = 1` for `z ≠ 0`, so `det R_s = 1` and `R_sᵀ R_s = 1`.

E2.name: FRC.Fourier.rot_mul
E2.doc: 6:E2 — `s ↦ R_s` is a homomorphism of the meridian cycle: `R_{s+r} = R_s R_r` reads `rot (z w) = rot z * rot w` for `z = g^{−s}`, `w = g^{−r}`.

E2.name: FRC.Fourier.unitsEquivCircle
E2.doc: 6:E2 — the circle is the unit group: `u ↦ (c_u, d_u)` with inverse `(c, d) ↦ c + i d`, so `SO(2, K) ≃ K^×` when `K` has a quarter-turn.

E2.name: FRC.Fourier.card_circle
E2.doc: 6:E2 — `|SO(2, K)| = |K| − 1` for a finite field with a quarter-turn: the rotation group of the `p²`-point plane has `p − 1 = 4κ` elements, the size of the meridian cycle.

E5.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_spectral_obstruction
E5.doc: 6:E5 — the spectral obstruction: the shift has every unit of `𝔽_p` as an eigenvalue (eigenvector `(a^j)_j`), the family at most four; for `κ ≥ 2` no invertible `T` conjugates `σ` to `F^{[s]}`.

E6.name: FRC.Fourier.frft_mul_proj_one
E6.doc: 6:E6 — the character sector: on `im Π_1` the family acts by the meridian character, `F^{[s]} Π_1 = z^{s} Π_1`; the intertwiner `F^{[s]} (x Π_1 v) = Π_1 ((z^s x) v)` is linearity.

E6.name: FRC.Fourier.rot_eigenline
E6.doc: 6:E6 — the eigenline: `R_s (1, −i)ᵀ = z (1, −i)ᵀ`, the same character `z = g^{−s}` (Prop. charsector).

E7.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_heisenberg
E7.doc: 6:E7 — on every shell: `F σ = D_1 F` and `F D_1 = σ⁻¹ F`, with `σ σ⁻¹ = 1`.
